item.title: Alternative Proteins for Sustainable and Ethical Food Systems: Consumer, Production, and Supply-Chain Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
Sina Ahmadi Kaliji, Università di Bologna

Margo Degieter, Ghent University

Hans De Steur, Ghent University

Luca Camanzi, Università di Bologna

Marleen Onwezen, Wageningen University and Research

The global food system faces mounting pressures from climate change, biodiversity loss, and sustainability concerns. Alternative proteins such as cultured meat, plant-based options, insect-based products, and novel dairy substitutes offer potential solutions. However, understanding how these alternatives reshape the broader food system remains incomplete, as existing research often examines consumption, production, and regulation in isolation without addressing value-chain restructuring, producer adoption, and governance.

This special issue seeks integrated research bridging consumer perspectives with production and supply-chain dynamics, addressing how individual decisions interact with system-level factors like regulations and policies. Contributions should explore producer decision-making, market development, environmental and animal-welfare implications, regulatory environments, and economic feasibility of alternative protein systems. The collection aims to generate actionable insights for policymakers and industry stakeholders navigating sustainable protein transitions.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer acceptance and willingness to pay for alternative proteins
  • Farm-level decision-making and economic feasibility
  • Sustainability and life-cycle assessments of alternative protein supply chains
  • Regulatory frameworks, certification and labelling
  • Cultural, ethical and societal narratives
  • Communication and trust-building strategies
  • Cultured meat production systems
  • Plant-based meat analogues
  • Insect-based foods and products
  • Alternative dairy products
  • Animal welfare implications
  • Supply-chain coordination and value-chain restructuring
  • Rural livelihoods and producer adoption
  • Market development and price formation
  • Individual versus system-level dynamics
  • Policy implications for protein transitions
